newsitem.title: TAIWAN: HK protest ship to arrive in Taiwan early Friday.
newsitem.headline: HK protest ship to arrive in Taiwan early Friday.

text.p: A Hong Kong ship that ended a ill-fated protest trip to disputed East China Sea islands on Thursday was expected to arrive in Taiwan's northern Keelung port early Friday, Taiwanese state radio said.
"The ship will arrive at 1:45 tomorrow morning (1745 GMT Thursday) at the earliest," the radio quoted Keelung port officials as saying.
The rusty Kien Hwa 2 ended its mission in tragedy when protest leader David Chan drowned after leaping into the sea near the islands as a symbolic challenge to Japan's claim of sovereignty.
The islands are known as the Senkakus in Japan and the Diaoyus in China, Taiwan and Hong Kong.
"We will let them (activists) come in and help them fly back to Hong Kong later," port official Hsu Kuo-ching said on the radio.
A wave of protests has swept Hong Kong, Taiwan, Macau and China since July, when Japanese ultranationalists built a lighthouse and raised Japanese flags on the islands to assert Tokyo's sovereignty.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule in mid-1997 and many Hong Kong people see the dispute as a test of China's strength and integrity.

Chan's group sailed out of Hong Kong on Sunday intending to rip down the lighthouse and flags and to plant a People's Republic of China red communist flag, claiming the islands as Chinese sovereign territory.
Taiwan, considered a renegade province by China, also claims the archipelago.

Taiwan's state-run Central News Agency earlier quoted unnamed navigation officials as saying Taipei would allow Kien Hwa 2 to dock on humanitarian grounds even if it flies China's flag. But a second official contacted at Keelung insisted the flag must not fly at the bow.
